correctness.rationale: For constant-control six-compartment compliant/noncompliant SIR equations in Ngo–Parkinson–Wang version 3, summing all six equations forces K=b/delta and summing the three noncompliant equations fixes N*=u uniquely as positive root of q u²+(nu+delta-qK)u-xi b=0. With m=q u fixed, the susceptible 2x2 matrix M(lambda) is an irreducible nonsingular M-matrix with strictly positive inverse; S(lambda),S*(lambda) decrease strictly because d/dlambda=-M^-1 diag(1-alpha,1)(S,S*). The infected transfer matrix V^-1 is strictly positive and self-consistency becomes F(lambda)=beta(P S(lambda)+Q S*(lambda))/J=1, where F(0)=Rinv and F tends to zero. Thus a unique positive scalar lambda (hence positive all six compartments) exists exactly when Rinv>1. Clearing denominator gives the specified quadratic with leading coefficient J(1-alpha)>0. The published printed ratio is demonstrably different from actual next-generation Rinv but is not a new finding. Independent Fraction calculation verified every six-equation residual of the exact (1900/3901,379/85822,366/42911,3775/7802,340/42911,353/42911) witness, lambda=1/25. All-parameter claim relies on M-matrix/monotonic proof, not samples.
